answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may post jobs or claim rewards, with voting weight and rate limits tied to the locked amount rather than the number of accounts. Splitting funds across a thousand sybils then grants no extra influence, while each account still incurs setup and monitoring overhead. To overwhelm the system, an attacker must acquire and lock substantially more capital, which is costly and remains exposed to slashing for provable fraud. A mesa of agents can coordinate a voyage, but cannot mint pigment into collateral.
